newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wool prices firm at New Zealand sales.
newsitem.headline: Wool prices firm at New Zealand sales.

text.p: Wool prices continued to improve at Thursday's Christchurch and Napier sales, the market indicator gaining seven cents to 455 NZ cents per kg clean, Wools of New Zealand said.
The strong segment indicator firmed eight cents to 389, the medium segment fell 22 cents to 565 cents and the lamb segment rose by eight to 412 cents.
New Zealand exporters said the main bidding came from local mills, Western Europe, China and Nepal with support from Turkey Australia, India and Pakistan.
Of the 4,683 clean tonnes on offer, 15 percent was passed in.
The offer comprised 42 percent second shear, 24 percent crossbred fleece, nine percent lambswool and six percent halfbred fleece.
Compared to the May 8 Napier sale, prices for 36 micron crossbred fleece were 2.5-3.0 percent cheaper while 37 micron was 2-4 percent dearer.

Second shear was 3 percent dearer, cotts 5 percent dearer, first lambs 2 percent dearer, second lambs unchanged, bulky skirtings, bellies and pieces 3-5 percent dearer and crutchings 5 percent dearer.
Merino fleece was 5 percent dearer than in the May 1 Christchurch sale and halfbred fleece 2-3 percent cheaper.
The next sale is scheduled for Napier on June 5.
